symptom: The shipped ProductionRun driver tests fail because legacy jobs are treated as retired instead of progressing through sample-gate, pause, QA, and trust contracts.
direct_cause: The cutover driver intercepts submit_intent_persisted legacy jobs with a retirement needs_attention result and no longer follows the main-branch legacy progression semantics.
class_root: Legacy-playbook generation remains an active product contract until the M2 replacement is shipped; route ownership must distinguish active legacy execution from the future retirement assertion without changing its current behavior.
affected_population: Existing projects with persisted legacy ProductionRun jobs
ProductionRun sample-gate, pause/resume, QA verification, and trust-level flows
entry_points: production sample-gate, pause/resume, QA, and trust-level callers
internal_only_reason: The failure is an application route-ownership invariant; no third-party dependency controls it.
invariants: Persisted legacy-playbook jobs continue through the shipped driver state machine.
Retirement assertions are tracked as an M2 red light and do not silently alter M1 legacy behavior.
generality_proof: All checked legacy callers converge on driveGeneration and its shared state transitions; restoring that boundary covers persisted jobs regardless of which gate or trust policy caused the next transition.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the active legacy-playbook state machine and its sample, pause, QA, and authorization transitions.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The sample-gate suite drives the shared driver with persisted legacy jobs and observes its next state.
The pause suite reaches the same driver boundary through a different lifecycle state and requires resumable legacy behavior.
QA approval is another shared-driver transition after legacy generation.
Trust policy changes authorization state but still enters the same legacy driver.

recurrence.reason: Any persisted legacy job, gate state, trust policy, or future caller can encounter the cutover retirement interception.
same_class_scan: Checked productionRunDriver, productionSampleGate, productionRunPauseSemantics, productionQaVerify, and productionTrustLevel suites.

prevention.invariant: The active legacy route must not emit a retirement result before the M2 replacement owns that route.
prevention.failure_mode: Invalid state still follows the existing visible gate/error contract; it is never silently treated as retired.
prevention.strategy: Keep route ownership at the shared driver and record retirement expectations separately as an M2 red light until the replacement is ready.

legacy_paths.rationale: The legacy route is intentionally retained as active product behavior; only its retired assertions move to M2 documentation.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency controls the ProductionRun state-machine contract.

migration: No runtime migration is performed in M1. The retired assertions and their expected future completion criteria move to the M2 red-light section.
residual_risks: M2 must ship the replacement generation route and then satisfy the documented retirement assertions.
